steps.desc: Build all debug workspace targets in one Cargo invocation
steps.description: ONE-FAT-BUILD 2026-08-04 (task collapse-separate-build-nodes-into-one-fat-cargo-invocation): one cargo build owns the complete debug workspace graph, including test targets and the flaky harness. This removes the redundant flaky-harness build node. preferred_inner_jobs=32 is measured on a cold empty target at hermit@846baeca: 130.35s, cgroup-recorded peak=11663998976 bytes. The generous 64GiB cap deliberately prioritizes throughput over cap tightness. Release artifacts remain a separate profile because Cargo cannot emit dev and release profiles in one invocation; the privileged lane is a separate DAG and is unchanged.

steps.desc: Build release Hermit and all runtime backend artifacts in one Cargo invocation
steps.description: ONE-FAT-BUILD 2026-08-04: this is the dependency-driven exception to the debug fat build. DBT, SaBRe, and LiteInst tests require target/release/hermit and release plugins, while ordinary tests consume debug targets. One release Cargo invocation now sees hermit, detcore-dbt, detcore-sabre, and hermit-install together; the former serial dbt_release+sabre_release invocations are gone. preferred_inner_jobs=32 is measured on a cold empty target at hermit@846baeca: 185.423s, cgroup-recorded peak=9006452736 bytes. The copied binary lets the strict-compat DAG node use the Rust driver's explicit-prebuilt contract rather than rebuilding the same release profile.
steps.cmd: HERMIT_INSTALL_FORCE_RESTAGE=${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}-runtime ./ci/run-with-reverie-dbt-budget.sh cargo build --release --locked -p hermit --features third-party-backends -p detcore-dbt -p detcore-sabre -p hermit-install && mkdir -p target/ci && install -m 755 target/release/hermit target/ci/hermit-strict && sha256sum target/install_pkg/rsrcs/sabre && cat target/install_pkg/rsrcs/sabre.revision

steps.desc: Build and stage the release LiteInst runtime
Build the manifest-plan binaries the metadata validation runs
steps.description: MOVED OUT OF e2e.metadata 2026-08-08. e2e.metadata is a DAG ROOT whose first action is `cargo run -p hermit-manifest-plan` -- twice: load_tests uses the default bin, audit_test_footprints uses generate-test-footprints. It therefore COMPILES, upstream of every build node. That made the old metadata budget BIMODAL: 16.5s warm, 57s cold, 2 slow in 9 sampled CI runs. The compile remains HERE under a build-shaped budget so metadata inherits a warm artifact. The later 180s metadata budget is independent: by 2026-08-09 the non-build audit workload itself consumed 71.44-73.84s wall and 58.36-60.38s CPU across three warm samples, exceeding the former 60s ceiling even after this compile split.

steps.desc: Validate E2E metadata, generated test footprints, and required-cell plan
steps.description: MEASURED 2026-08-09 at hermit 93575493 after the Rust validate cutover: the warm audit-ci subroutine completed in 71.44s, 72.11s, and 73.84s wall (58.36-60.38s CPU), and the complete command passed in 73.77s. The former 60s ceiling was therefore below intrinsic CPU demand, not detecting a hang. The host was loaded (load 78.58 on 316 CPUs; CPU PSI some 5.74%), but CPU time alone reached the ceiling and all samples made forward progress through footprint generation, splitter, inventory, and correspondence checks. 180s preserves >2.4x headroom for observed host variance without changing the command or hiding failures; a real hang still terminates and records a timeout.

steps.desc: DynamoRIO DBT strict backend parity matrix
Portable working-envelope levels (L1-L4 over true/echo/date; implemented by scripts/validate.rs)
steps.cmd: set -e; HERMIT=target/debug/hermit; ARGS='run --base-env=minimal --no-virtualize-cpuid --max-timeslice=disabled'; REPS=${L4_REPS:-20}; run_probe() { local c="$1"; timeout 30s $HERMIT $ARGS --strict -- $c </dev/null; timeout 30s $HERMIT $ARGS --strict --verify -- $c </dev/null; timeout 30s $HERMIT $ARGS --strict --verify --detlog-heap --detlog-stack -- $c </dev/null; local i; for ((i=0;i<REPS;i++)); do timeout 30s $HERMIT $ARGS --strict --verify -- $c </dev/null; done; }; run_probe '/bin/true'; run_probe '/bin/echo hermit-envelope'; run_probe '/bin/date -u +%Y'
